title: [review] DRX2/DAD1 persistence: document tamper/rollback boundary (CRC32 detects corruption, not tampering)
description: P2 disposition-bead, wave-3 security review. lichen-hal/src/storage.rs:47-75 slot integrity is CRC32 only; generation u64 lives inside the record it orders, so an attacker with flash-write access can (a) roll back BOTH slots, (b) delete the newer slot so open_redundant picks the old one, or (c) forge a minimal record (origin_sequence=1 floor, recompute CRC) -> open_root trusts it as high-water and replay checks accept captured signature-valid DAOs as fresh. Bounded: same flash-write capability already means total compromise (identity keys live there too); format is explicitly provisional/unshipped. Disproportionate fixes rejected. FIX (in scope): document the boundary in persistence.rs/storage.rs module docs: DRX2/DAD1 provide corruption detection, NOT tamper resistance; anti-rollback anchor is physical flash possession. Optionally note the defense-in-depth path (device-key MAC + independent monotonic NVS counter) as future work. Do NOT implement the MAC now.
